stories.headline: WRECKAGE VIEWED; Naval Survey Will Be Limited to Interests of Government; TWO OTHER INQUIRIES; Department of Commerce Will Study Cause of Accident to the HindenBurg; REICH GROUP ON WAY HERE; Sabotage Theory Discarded --Passenger and Officer Succumb to Injuries
stories.summary: The German airship Hindenburg crashed, and while sabotage is a possibility, it has been largely discarded as a cause, with the Department of Commerce set to study the accident

stories.headline: CABINET IN SESSION; All German Navy Craft Wait With Steam Up for Instructions LONDON MEETING CALLED Non - Intervention Group to Consider Safety Measures for Warships Off Spain SPANISH LINER IS SUNK Vessel With Heavy Passenger List Is Torpedoed by Rebel Submarine Off Barcelona "Measures" Not Divulged TEXT OF COMMUNIQUE SPANISH BOMBING STIRS THE REICH Serious Crisis for Reich Demand on London Likely News of Bombing Delayed Ambassador Davies Visits Parents' Home in Wales European Action Demanded Valencia Officials Silent Battleship Reaches Gibraltar Rebels Torpedo a Liner
stories.summary: A Spanish liner was torpedoed by a rebel submarine off Barcelona, and the German Navy is on high alert, as the international community considers safety measures for warships off Spain

stories.headline: YOUNGSTOWN STEEL MILLS WILL CLOSE, IF MEN STRIKE, UNTIL THEY ASK JOBS BACK; SEEK A 'SHOWDOWN' Two Independents Plan to End Threat of Closed Shop Now UNION IS NOT ASKING ONE But Republic and Youngstown Sheet and Tube Bar Contract as Opening Wedge DISCRIMINATION CHARGED S. W. O. C. Asserts Union Men Suffer Lay-Offs--Walkout Is Held 'Inevitable' Day's Strike Developments Talk of Steel Shutdown 33,000 in Youngstown 2 STEEL COMPANIES PLAN 'SHOWDOWN' Conditions Held Different Prepared for Strike Discrimination Charged 'PEACE OR WAR' IN VOTE S. W. O. C. Leaders Stress Issue in Jones & Laughlin Ballot
stories.summary: Youngstown steel mills are set to close if workers strike, as Republic and Youngstown Sheet and Tube companies plan to end the threat of a closed shop, with the union stressing 'peace or war' as a slogan in an upcoming vote

stories.headline: ROYAL TITLE DENIED TO WINDSOR'S BRIDE; King Orders That Mrs. Warfield Shall Not Be Styled as 'Her Royal Highness' VICTORIA SET PRECEDENT Ministers Gave 'Advice' in the Recognition of Status to Duke, but Excluding His Wife Emphasis on Word "Only" ROYAL TITLE DENIED TO WINDSOR'S BRIDE Victory for Court Group Ministerial Responsibility Vagueness on Old Document Act Will Stop Speculation EDWARD ANGERED BY NEWS Refuses to Accept Defeat as Final, Associate Reports DUKE RE-ENGAGES DRIVER Reported to Have Phoned Him to Serve on Wedding Trip
stories.summary: King Edward has denied his bride, Wallis Warfield, the title of 'Her Royal Highness', following precedent set by Queen Victoria, in a decision that has angered the Duke of Windsor

rounds.blurb: The Hindenburg crashed, with the Department of Commerce investigating the cause. The German Navy was on high alert due to a rebel submarine torpedoing a Spanish liner. Labor disputes also escalated in Youngstown steel mills.

stories.headline: THANT OPENS TALKS WITH CASTRO ON VERIFYING MISSILES' REMOVAL; U.S. HALTS SURVEILLANCE FROM AIR; 2D MEETING TODAY Havana Reports No Accord--U.N. Calls Session 'Useful' Thant Opens Discussions With Castro on Verifying Removal of Soviet Missiles CUBANS REPORT NO AGREEMENT But U.N. Aide Says Session Is 'Very Useful'--2d Meeting Due Today
stories.summary: U.N. Secretary-General U Thant met with Fidel Castro in Havana to discuss verifying the removal of Soviet missiles, with a second meeting scheduled, as the U.S. halted air surveillance during the talks. The meetings were described as 'useful' by a U.N. aide.

stories.headline: THANT'S CUBA TALKS 'FRUITFUL'; HE WILL FLY TO HAVANA TODAY; BLOCKADE HALTED DURING TRIP; AIR CHECK GOES ON Missile Sites Watched Despite Suspension of Quarantine U.S. Suspending Blockade of Cuba for Thant's Two Day Meeting With Castro AIR SURVEILLANCE OF BASES GOES ON Naval Units Remain in Area --Gesture Viewed as Aid to U.N. Chief in Talks
stories.summary: U.N. Secretary-General U Thant's talks with Fidel Castro were deemed 'fruitful', and the U.S. suspended its blockade of Cuba during Thant's two-day meeting, although air surveillance of missile sites continued. The move was seen as a gesture to aid Thant's talks.

stories.headline: MACMILLAN BIDS BRITAIN BECOME GUIDE OF EUROPE; Tory Party Told New Trade Group Can Be Influenced Toward a World Role NATION URGED TO GROW Premier Says Old Ways and Old Privileges Must Give Way to New Methods Too Set in Ways Common Market Hurdle MACMILLAN BIDS BRITAIN BE GUIDE Federal System Barred Spice for the Tories Political Ammunition
stories.summary: British Prime Minister Harold Macmillan urged the UK to become a guide for Europe and adapt to new methods, as the country considered its role in the European Common Market, with a focus on growth and changing trade patterns. Macmillan emphasized the need to move beyond old ways and privileges.

stories.headline: RECORD 3,442,410 QUALIFIED TO VOTE IN ELECTION HERE; Statewide Total Is Also Due to Set Mark for Eligibility in a Gubernatorial Year 5-DAY DRIVE ADDS 9.1% But Big Enrollment Is Not Interpreted as a Sign of Heavy Turnout at Polls Rise of 700,000 Over '58 Helped by Carry-Over RECORD 3,442,410 CAN VOTE IN CITY Size of Vote Weighed Actual Number Smaller
stories.summary: A record number of New Yorkers, 3,442,410, were qualified to vote in the upcoming election, following a 5-day registration drive that added 9.1% to the rolls, although the large enrollment was not expected to necessarily translate to a high turnout at the polls.

rounds.blurb: U.N. Secretary-General U Thant met with Fidel Castro to discuss verifying Soviet missile removal. The US halted air surveillance during talks and suspended its blockade of Cuba. Thant's efforts were deemed 'fruitful' and 'useful'.

stories.headline: WARSHIP'S PLANES START SEARCH FOR MISS EARHART; NO DEFINITE SIGNAL HEARD; COLORADO IN ACTION Director of Hunt Says Fliers' Fate Should Be Known Monday 104,000 SQ. MILES COVERED Itasca, Swan Have Scanned Area North of Howland--Lexington Speeds West PUTNAM STILL HOPEFUL Husband of Lost Flier Believes She May Be Found in Area Below Howland Islands Mysterious Signals Continue Expects to Know by Monday Lexington's Speed a Factor WARSHIP'S PLANES JOIN EARHART HUNT Putnam Keeps Up Hope Son to Join Putnam FROWN ON 'STUNT FLYING' WHERE EARHART PLANE IS BEING SOUGHT
stories.summary: Amelia Earhart's plane is missing and a search effort is underway, with her husband George Putnam remaining hopeful that she will be found, as warships and planes scour the area near the Howland Islands

stories.headline: ALLIANCE WINS DAY; Former Foes of Leader Desert Whalen to Join in Fight on New Deal SOME CHIEFS DEFIANT Hines and Kenneally Break With Organization to Side With 4 County Heads PRIMARY FIGHTS SURE County and District Contests Foreseen-Court Bill Defeat a Factor in Outcome Victory for Dooling Copeland Is Silent COPELAND VICTOR IN TAMMANY FIGHT Kennedy Acts for Dooling Court Plan Collapse a Factor Hines Explains Vote Some Delay at Start Call for Primary Read Alliance Is Confirmed Untermyer Backs Whalen
stories.summary: A power struggle within Tammany Hall has led to a shift in alliances, with some former foes of the leader joining forces to oppose the New Deal, and John F. Hines and other chiefs defecting to side with county heads

stories.headline: JAPANESE TAKE TWO TOWNS IN FIGHTING NEAR PEIPING; CHINESE PREPARE FOR WAR; PEACE MOVES FAIL Japan Is Suspected of Plan to Increase Hold on North China NANKING TROOPS ON MOVE Chiang Kai-shek Is Reported to Have Ordered His Air Force to Be Mobilized JAPAN SEES A BIG CHANCE Army Believes Soviet Forces in East Are Too Upset to Intervene Effectively The Chinese Situation Renewal of the Fighting Japanese Rush Troops JAPANESE CAPTURE 2 TOWNS IN CLASH Chinese Expected Attack More Japanese On Way U. S. Embassy Car Halted FIGHTING AT PEIPING
stories.summary: Japanese forces have taken two towns near Peiping, China, as fighting resumes and peace moves fail, with Chiang Kai-shek mobilizing his air force and the Japanese believing Soviet forces are too weakened to intervene

SEES LET-DOWN; UNION TOO 'SPEEDY' It Also Is Taking In Too Much Territory, Some at Capital Feel CABINET REMARKS CITED Roper and Perkins Views Are Taken by Labor to Mean 'Scuttling' of Drive ROBINSON TEST EXPECTED C. I. O., Opposing Him for Bench, May Open Attack by Effort to Link Him to Utilities Day's Labor Developments Roosevelt-Lewis Break Seen Miss Perkins's Actions Cited Washington saw a possibility of a break between the administration and John L. Lewis over the C. I. O.'s militant policies. Page 1. Secretary Roper, in an appeal for industrial peace, said the public will not tolerate extremists on either side. Page 6. Troops were on hand at Cleveland to keep peace as Republic Steel prepared to reopen four struck plants. Page 1. Johnstown officials believed that the C. I. O. had suffered a setback in failure of the crowd at the strike mass meeting there to live up to expectations. Page 5.
stories.summary: A potential break between the administration of President Franklin D. Roosevelt and John L. Lewis, leader of the C.I.O., is hinted at due to the union's militant policies, with some in the capital feeling that the C.I.O. is moving too quickly and taking in too much territory

rounds.blurb: Amelia Earhart's plane went missing, prompting a massive search effort near the Howland Islands. Japanese forces captured two towns near Peiping, China, as fighting resumed. A potential break between the Roosevelt administration and John L. Lewis was hinted at due to the C.I.O.'s militant policies.
